rules.sentence: A subphrenic abscess can lead to local and systemic complications, with any delay in diagnosis exacerbating these complications.
Intra-abdominal complications include generalized peritonitis, enteric fistulae, and ileus.
Thoracic complications include pleurisy, pleural effusion, empyema, lung abscess, or bronchial fistula.
Infection may progress to a multi-located or diffuse process or sepsis.
Early recognition, prompt resuscitation, targeted antimicrobial therapy, and effective drainage have collectively reduced mortality from 40% to 60% to approximately 18% to 30%.

However, patients with a prolonged intensive care course experience deconditioning and benefit from early physical, occupational, and speech therapy to restore strength, mobility, and overall functional status.
Respiratory therapy, including deep breathing exercises and early mobilization, plays a crucial role in recovery.
